answer.rationale: Finance demands an 18% cost cut; the incumbent has refused to move on price this cycle, so staying is not a viable cost path. Memory c2 records that a prior switch to the low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit-cost savings with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which directly addresses the cost mandate. Memory c6 shows that multi-year commitments can further unlock volume pricing, which could be layered onto the new vendor to deepen the saving. The primary contract expires in 14 days, so a decision must be made now; deferring or waiting is not an option. Adding a second source (c3) would protect against single-point-of-failure risk but does not itself cut unit cost enough to meet the 18% target and would consume the single decision slot. Renegotiating with the incumbent (c4) is moot because they have already refused to reopen price. The 94% line utilization with no buffer means delivery continuity is critical; c2's record of smooth, accurate onboarding mitigates that risk, but I will still require a short overlap window or expedited qualification before the incumbent contract lapses.
